cmc_note: CMC = expanded uncertainty at approximately 95 % confidence (k = 2). It excludes the unit under test (resolution, repeatability, drift); a certificate value may be larger.
source: Calibration Scope of Accreditation, Section V Electrical - DC/Low Frequency, pp. 8-32; Section XII Time & Frequency; coil lines pp. 9 and 30

entries.notes: Bands are by instrument RANGE (100 uA, 1/10/100 mA, 1 A, 3 A) and frequency; "rng" is a percentage of that range.

entries.standard: Precision multimeter or AC measurement standard
entries.notes: Bands are by the measured voltage (rms) and frequency.

entries.standard: Multifunction calibrator (both listed sets) / transconductance amplifier/coil
entries.notes: Coil lines added (p. 9 of 47, comment Transconductance amplifier/coil): (2 to 20) A 90 uA/A + 0.1 mA, (20 to 120) A 80 uA/A + 8 mA, (120 to 3000) A 0.8 % + 0.08 A.
Band CMC applies at every nominal; the scope fixed-point list is not used.

Capacitance relative terms are fractions of the value (percent given in the scope). Two scope groups: the first 8 lines (0.5 % + 0.01 nF ... 33 to 110 mF) are tagged src 5522A (they are the 5522A/5520A 1-year capacitance specification), the last 9 (0.19 % + 3.6 pF ... ) src 5560A; a point takes the line of the calibrator that sourced it (largest of both when the calibrator is unknown). The tag is an inference from the numbers - confirm.
Bands by the generated voltage (rms) and frequency; where two listed calibrator sets overlap the larger CMC is used.

entries.standard: Multifunction calibrator / transconductance amplifier / coil (Clamp-On Only: multifunction calibrator/coil)
entries.notes: Bands by the generated current and frequency (not by instrument range); overlapping sets: larger CMC used. Coil lines added (p. 30 of 47): (20.5 to 3000) A (16 to 850) Hz 0.7 % + 0.84 A and (0.85 to 6) kHz 0.8 % + 0.84 A (Transconductance amplifier/coil); Clamp-On Only (20.5 to 1025) A (45 to 65) Hz 0.8 %, (65 to 440) Hz 0.99 % (Multifunction calibrator/coil).
Thermocouple simulation, degC (printed p. 13 of 47, verified against the page image). bands = Type K; types = B C D E J K L N R S T U.
